resolutionSupport.reason: Full Swin encoder stride32 and decoder image-to-channel patch folding; attention windows and half-scale branch can pad independently.

input.kind: Local sRGB preview developed from user-provided RAW

method.processes: Each timed run launches a new native process and loads MLModel, performs one prediction and exits. No resident-model inference reused for the target.
method.requestDefinition: Monotonic time from MLModel load through PNG decode, CoreGraphics resize, prediction and validated Float32 alpha copy; output writes excluded.
notIncluded: Some system GPU/driver allocations in process RSS
method.cachePolicy: OS, CoreML and GPU caches not purged. First measurement after each new compiled model separated from subsequent fresh-process measurements.
method.concurrency: All model conversions and native runs sequential; lightweight image diagnostics only during conversion/reference phases.

runs.limitations: Fresh native process; OS/Core ML/GPU caches not purged. upperReference2048.scope: Previously qualified source from the same host; not remeasured with the new full-request instrumentation. Already far outside the requested band.

limitations: One image and one host; no ground-truth alpha and no guarantee of Lightroom equivalence.
The initial new-model request is substantially slower than the cache-populated median. Six seconds is not an upper-bound guarantee.
Changing resolution can alter fine edges and interior background gaps; visual comparison and final candidate reference parity required.
1920 maximum native-versus-FP32 alpha difference is0.50255 and1792 maximum0.20853; passing the existing gate does not establish pixel equality.
No new CPU timing matrix was run because the qualified CPU+GPU path reaches the target band; earlier CPU alternatives remain separate historical measurements.

1024.scope: Separate qualification process using the saved Pillow reference-input.png; these timings are excluded from the original-preview performance series.

1792.scope: Separate qualification process using the saved Pillow reference-input.png; these timings are excluded from the original-preview performance series.

1920.scope: Separate qualification process using the saved Pillow reference-input.png; these timings are excluded from the original-preview performance series.

driftControl1024.scope: Final separate control, not inserted into the fixed initial N=3 median. Inference stable; model-load variation accounts for most request-time change.

decisionNotes: 1920 is the largest newly tested side with median request in the approximate 5–7s target band; the contemporary 2048 control is clearly above it.

1792 also meets the band and has lower native/FP32 differences on its own exact reference input than 1920. This supports considering it as a conservative quality/time alternative, not a ground-truth quality score.
1920 and 1792 are experimental artifacts only; the approved 2048 app installation and backend selection are unchanged.
All initial N=3 performance outputs are byte-reproducible within each resolution, despite model-loader/cache timing variation.
privacy: No photograph, derivative, filename, local path or image/alpha hash is included.

visualInspection.method: Two native-preview-pixel crops covering fine needles and interior gaps; all sizes use the same source preview and CoreGraphics input resizing, including the new 2048 control. Scalar alpha restored to original aspect, then linear-sRGB background exposure -5 EV, contrast 0.
observations: 1920 and 1792 preserve inspected needle tips and interior gaps very similarly to the current 2048 comparison; no clear systematic detail loss was visible in these crops.
Thin bright mixed-pixel edges remain under -5 EV at every inspected size, including 2048.
visualInspection.limitations: Single photograph and two crops, no ground-truth alpha; does not cancel native/FP32 differences or replace production-renderer validation.
